clue.text: It could go up in the depression

definitions.text: It could go up in the depression

parts.words: It could go up in the depression
parts.note: a depression sounds economic or emotional, but here it is a weather low bringing rain, when this item is opened and raised overhead

explanation.surface: Something that might rise during an economic slump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' tempts towards economics or mood; it is the meteorological sense, an area of low pressure that brings rain.
explanation.definitionFit: A rain shield is put up when a low-pressure system brings wet weather.

clue.text: One with a telling part in play

definitions.text: One with a telling part in play

parts.words: One with a telling part in play
parts.note: a 'telling part' sounds like a significant role, but it means a role that tells the story to the audience

explanation.surface: An actor whose role in a play is a significant one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Telling' usually means significant; here it is literal, the character who tells the tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A storyteller figure in a drama speaks to the audience to relate the plot.

clue.text: He has main control

parts.note: the main is an old word for the open sea, so control of the main is command at sea

explanation.surface: Someone who holds the principal authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' reads as 'chief', but in poetry and crosswords 'the main' is the ocean, so this is a naval commander.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior naval officer commands a fleet on the ocean.

clue.text: Diffident in two ways

parts.note: a mode is a way of doing something
ST is short for street, and a street is a way

explanation.surface: Being shy in two different respects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two ways' supplies both pieces: MODE (a manner) and ST (street, an abbreviation for a road or way).
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone shy and unassuming about themselves.

clue.text: Not off upon a visit, but ready to make one

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed upon another sits above it in the grid

parts.note: a switch that is not off is on
a call is a short visit paid to someone

explanation.surface: A doctor not off duty, available to make a house visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upon' puts ON above CALL in this down entry; 'one' in the definition refers back to a visit.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor available for duty is prepared to go out to a patient when summoned.

clue.text: Wedding invitation to officiating clergyman?

parts.note: read as words a couple might say to the priest, asking him to unite them in marriage

explanation.surface: A card inviting the vicar to a marriage ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: A wedding invitation usually asks guests to attend; here the request is that the priest perform the joining in matrimony.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a friendly invitation, and a couple would literally ask the minister to unite them.

clue.text: Dangerous condition of an author after shocking reviews?

definitions.text: Dangerous condition of an author after shocking reviews?

parts.words: Dangerous condition of an author after shocking reviews?
parts.note: a medical phrase for grave sickness, read jokingly as a writer made sick by hostile critics

explanation.surface: A writer left in a bad way by terrible press notices.
explanation.walkthrough: The medical phrase is reread: the writer is sickened by the critics' harsh words.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means gravely sick in hospital terms, and punningly describes someone sickened by critics.

clue.text: Clean up management and succeed completely

parts.note: to sweep is to clean a floor with a brush
the board is the group of directors running a company

explanation.surface: A shake-up of company bosses described in housekeeping terms.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to win everything on offer, like a gambler taking all the stakes.

clue.text: Beauty consultant goes to the wall

definitions.text: Beauty consultant goes to the wall

parts.words: Beauty consultant goes to the wall
parts.note: 'goes to the wall' sounds like business failure, but the glass consulted for one's looks hangs on a wall

explanation.surface: A cosmetics adviser whose business collapses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes to the wall' means going bust; here it is literal, the looking-glass you consult about your appearance being hung up.
explanation.definitionFit: A looking-glass is what one consults about appearance, and it is often hung up indoors.

clue.text: Repeats the treatise needs amending

indicators.note: a text that needs amending will have its letters altered, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A complaint that a scholarly treatise must be corrected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needs amending' rearranges the letters of TREATISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean says or does again, over and over.

clue.text: Ventilate bearing

definitions.meaning: to let fresh breeze through a room

explanation.surface: Airing a room while bearing up.
explanation.definitionFit: To ventilate is to freshen with draughts; one's bearing is one's manner or demeanour.

clue.text: Shrinking flower?

parts.note: recalls the idiom for a very shy person, taken as a literal bloom

explanation.surface: A bloom that seems to wilt or shrink away.
explanation.walkthrough: A very shy person is called a 'shrinking' one of these; the clue takes the idiom literally.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a small purple plant, and the idiom pairs it with shyness.

clue.text: Open late perhaps for the supply of chamois

indicators.note: 'perhaps' says these letters are one possible arrangement among others

explanation.surface: A shop opening late to sell chamois leathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' rearranges OPEN LATE. Chamois leather originally came from a mountain animal of the goat-antelope family.
explanation.definitionFit: The chamois is a mountain goat-antelope whose skin gave the soft leather.

clue.text: It may be pierced, or just pricked

definitions.text: It may be pierced, or just pricked

parts.words: It may be pierced, or just pricked
parts.note: a body part that is pierced for jewellery, or pricked up when a person or animal listens

explanation.surface: Something that can be stabbed through or just jabbed.
explanation.walkthrough: Earrings need a piercing, and listeners 'prick up' this organ.
explanation.definitionFit: This hearing organ's lobe is pierced for jewellery and animals raise it when alert.

clue.text: Ghastly appearance of horse without carriage

indicators.note: 'without' in its old sense of outside: the horse goes around the carriage

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
a cab was a horse-drawn hired carriage

explanation.surface: A horse seen with no carriage behind it looks eerie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking; a solver reading it as 'minus' would look for something to delete and find nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something gruesome and horrifying, especially concerned with death.

clue.text: Keep out of the company of lawyers

definitions.meaning: barristers as a body, called to practise in court

explanation.surface: An instruction to steer clear of solicitors.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclude is to bar, and barristers collectively form the legal profession called the Bar.

clue.text: Famous treaty of 1713? The curt solution is here

indicators.note: a solution is a dissolving and remixing, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A history question whose terse answer is located here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solution' rearranges THE CURT. The Peace of 1713 ending the War of the Spanish Succession was signed in this Dutch city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch city gave its name to the 1713 peace treaties.

clue.text: Compositions that call for assurance of touch

definitions.text: Compositions that call for assurance of touch

parts.words: Compositions that call for assurance of touch
parts.note: keyboard showpieces needing a confident touch; the name comes from the Italian verb meaning to touch

explanation.surface: Pieces of music demanding a confident technique.
explanation.walkthrough: The name derives from Italian toccare, 'to touch', and such pieces show off a player's dexterity.
explanation.definitionFit: These are virtuoso keyboard pieces, named from the Italian word for touching.

clue.text: Bursting out into pure chaos

indicators.note: letters thrown into chaos are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Something breaking out into utter disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chaos' rearranges INTO PURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcano's outburst or a sudden breaking out of anger is described this way.

clue.text: Criticises VAT, say

indicators.note: 'say' tells us the phrase is spoken and heard as a similar-sounding word

parts.note: Value Added Tax is a tax, giving the phrase 'a tax'

explanation.surface: Grumbling about the sales tax.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT, the UK sales tax, is 'a tax'; 'say' means speaking that phrase, which sounds like a word for criticises.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay into someone verbally is to criticise them harshly.

clue.text: Get over unkind act, that's plain to see

parts.note: to clear a hurdle is to get over it
a cut is a snub, deliberately ignoring someone

explanation.surface: Advice to move past someone's unkindness.
explanation.definitionFit: Something definite and obvious, leaving no doubt.

clue.text: Lively turn I've put on

parts.note: a turn is a performer's act in a variety show
taken without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: A lively variety turn that the speaker has staged.
explanation.walkthrough: The page's 'tum' is an OCR misreading of 'turn', a performer's act; 'put on' is the link, as one puts on a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe someone energetic and on the go.

clue.text: Cycle enclosure

definitions.meaning: a ring or area enclosed, as of stones

explanation.surface: A bike pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A cycle is a repeating round, and a ring can also mean an area enclosed.

clue.text: My little bits

definitions.meaning: small fragments, as of bread or cake

explanation.surface: A speaker pointing to their own small scraps.
explanation.definitionFit: 'My!' and this word are both mild exclamations of surprise; small fragments of bread are also called this.

clue.text: Credit, we hear, can be painful

indicators.note: 'we hear' marks a word heard rather than written, a sound-alike

parts.note: 'on tick' means on credit, so tick is credit

explanation.surface: Buying on credit may cause financial pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On tick' is British slang for on credit. The facial nerve condition tic douloureux is very painful, hence the loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An involuntary twitch, and the facial neuralgia called tic douloureux is notably agonising.

clue.text: A queenly carriage?

parts.note: a four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage was named after the 19th-century British monarch

explanation.surface: A royal coach, or a regal bearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carriage' could mean posture; it is the light horse-drawn carriage named after the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: The low four-wheeled carriage was named in honour of the long-reigning queen.

clue.text: Lost, as a dog may be

definitions.meaning: a homeless wandering dog is a stray, giving the split phrase 'a stray'

explanation.surface: A lost dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Gone off course is the first sense; read as two words it describes a dog without a home.

clue.text: One has to be uncommonly rich to do so

definitions.text: One has to be uncommonly rich to do so

parts.words: One has to be uncommonly rich to do so
parts.note: uncommonly suggests unusually, but it means not a commoner: a noble with lavish living

explanation.surface: A remark that luxury living takes exceptional wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncommonly' is a pun: unusually, and not a commoner, i.e. a peer.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to live in great luxury, like an aristocrat.
